dispute.a: Roadmap writers who count the platinum inside the 200-hour estimate say the last collectible grind, not the story, sets the real finish time.
dispute.b: Checklist writers who time the story and side content separately say a focused player finishes well under that estimate.
dispute.call: We budget about 200 hours and treat the estimate as a planning ceiling, not a promise - your last grind decides it.

trophies.guide: The platinum unlocks the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned. Nothing here has its own task: work the roadmap in order, keep the one possibly-missable trophy safe in Chapter 1, and let this pop last.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

steps.text: Confirm the full list first: 55 trophies in total - 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver and 46 bronze - so this one needs the other 54.
Follow the roadmap order in this guide: story first, then stranger strands, then the counted grinds, then 100 percent, then the finale trophy.
Protect the single possibly-missable trophy, Positive Mental Attitude, before Chapter 1 closes; everything else can be cleaned up later.
Keep one master save before the final mission so any ending-adjacent cleanup stays reachable without a replay.
Track 100 percent completion alongside the trophy list, because A Long Road overlaps most of the counted work.
Use the count steppers in this tracker for the long grinds instead of memory; the totals come from the official descriptions.
Cross-check your earned count against the official list whenever a session ends; a missed sync is easier to spot early.
Leave the two gold trophies - the final mission and 100 percent - as your last two targets before the platinum.
When the 54th trophy pops, this platinum follows automatically in the same session; no menu action is needed.
If it does not pop, reload the master save and re-earn the most recent trophy; list trackers agree this is a sync issue, not a second requirement.
Screenshot your platinum moment from the trophy card, not the in-game banner, if you want the official name and grade recorded.

dispute.a: One walkthrough treats Gone Fishing as a pure tutorial with no fail state worth planning for.
dispute.b: Another notes an early chase beat that can fail and restart a checkpoint, costing a few minutes.
dispute.call: Either way it is the opening mission and cannot be missed; play it through and do not restart the game over it.

trophies.guide: The opening mission of the game. Play through Gone Fishing at the very start of a new game and this bronze pops at the mission-complete screen; it cannot be missed.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise

steps.text: Start a new game and play the prologue sequence; Gone Fishing is the first full mission the story gives you.
Follow the on-screen prompts through the fishing trip setup - they double as the movement and interaction tutorial.
Stay with your partner during the boat segment and complete each marked objective in order.
When the trip turns, use cover as the game prompts you; this is the first shooting lesson and it is forgiving.
Drive back when the objective updates and let the closing cutscene play out in full.
The trophy pops on the mission-complete screen for Gone Fishing; it is hidden on PSN until earned, which is normal.
Do not skip the closing cutscene on a first playthrough - later Chapter 1 context builds directly on it.
Before pushing deeper into Chapter 1, note that this chapter holds the game's one possibly-missable window; see Positive Mental Attitude.
If the mission fails at the chase beat, the checkpoint restart is short; no trophy progress is lost.
After it pops, the free-roam map opens in stages - a good moment to start the tracker and mark this earned.
Completion here also starts the Chapter 1 completion count toward Paradise Lost.

dispute.a: One chapter guide ends Chapter 1 at the Cartel Heist aftermath.
dispute.b: Another counts one further short mission as the chapter's true closer before the Chapter 2 banner appears.
dispute.call: We treat the chapter banner on screen as the finish line: when the game says Chapter 2, Chapter 1 is done either way.

trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 1. The trophy pops when the chapter closes, right before the story moves on; story progress cannot be missed, only delayed.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost

steps.text: Work the Chapter 1 mission markers in order: Gone Fishing, Breakfast Run and the build-up to The Cartel Heist.
Complete Breakfast Run when it appears; it is a required Chapter 1 story mission, not a side activity.
Before starting The Cartel Heist, finish the Chapter 1 meditation spots for Positive Mental Attitude - its window closes as this chapter ends.
Use any free-roam gaps in Chapter 1 to visit the early meditation spots near the coast; they are quickest now.
Keep both protagonists' phone contacts answered; Chapter 1 gates a couple of missions behind a call.
Play The Cartel Heist when ready - it is the chapter's set-piece and its completion moves the story forward.
Watch for the chapter-close banner after the heist fallout; the trophy pops as Chapter 1 formally ends.
This trophy is PSN-hidden until earned, so its absence from a public list mid-chapter is expected.
If you reached the heist without the meditations done, reload a pre-heist save rather than pushing into Chapter 2.
Roadmaps agree Chapter 1 is short; finishing it cleanly with the missable safe is worth more than rushing it.
Once Chapter 2 opens, mark Paradise Lost earned and move the tracker filter to the next stage.

dispute.a: One structure guide opens Chapter 2 with the fallout missions only.
dispute.b: Another counts a free-roam interlude mission as the chapter's true first task.
dispute.call: Follow the mission markers in the order the game presents them; the chapter trophy only cares about the closing banner.

trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 2. The trophy pops at the chapter's closing banner; like all chapter trophies it is story-gated and cannot be missed.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money

steps.text: Begin Chapter 2 from the banner after Chapter 1 closes and work its mission markers in order.
Complete Child's Play during this chapter; it is a required story mission and carries its own trophy.
Expect the wanted system tutorial beats here; finish them as scripted rather than fighting the escalation.
Use Chapter 2 free-roam gaps to start stranger strands - several open now and pay off chapters later.
Start Andy's and Kenton's strands when their markers appear so their final missions land before the endgame.
Keep a rolling save at each new chapter banner; it is your insurance for any window you later learn about.
Play the chapter's closing mission when the marker chain converges; the trophy pops at the Chapter 3 banner.
The name carries asterisks on PSN exactly as shown here; trackers that sanitise it are showing the same trophy.
Chapter trophies are hidden on PSN until earned - do not read a blank card as a bug.
Difficulty does not affect any chapter trophy; play on the setting you enjoy.
After the banner, update the tracker: Chapter 2 done, and the strand finals move up the roadmap.

dispute.a: One chapter guide treats Headliners as the chapter's midpoint.
dispute.b: Another treats VCIA Takedown as the midpoint and Headliners as late-chapter.
dispute.call: The order inside the chapter does not change the trophy; play the markers as they unlock and the banner settles it.

trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 3, including Headliners and VCIA Takedown. The trophy pops at the closing banner and cannot be missed.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!

steps.text: Start Chapter 3 from its banner and follow the mission chain; Headliners and VCIA Takedown sit inside this chapter.
Complete Headliners when it unlocks - it carries the DWNFALL trophy as well as chapter progress.
Complete VCIA Takedown at the airport; it also sets up the unscheduled-departure trophy for later.
Use Chapter 3 downtime at the shooting range; the 42 gold challenges are easier learned in batches.
Keep stranger strands moving between story missions so no strand final collides with the finale.
Save at the chapter banner as usual; Chapter 3's close is a natural audit point for counts.
Play the closing mission chain to the Chapter 4 banner; the trophy pops there.
Hidden on PSN until earned, like every chapter trophy.
Check your 100 percent screen at this point: story percentage should match the chapters finished.
Roadmaps place the platinum's halfway time inside this chapter for most players.
Mark the chapter earned and shift the tracker to the Chapter 4 stage.

dispute.a: One structure guide counts four chapters plus a short epilogue.
dispute.b: Another folds the epilogue missions into Chapter 4 itself.
dispute.call: For the trophy it makes no difference: finish Chapter 4's banner, then keep playing - the final mission is its own trophy either way.

trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 4, including Operation Savage Glory. The trophy pops at the chapter's end; the final mission itself is tracked separately as a gold trophy.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma

steps.text: Enter Chapter 4 from its banner and work the mission chain toward Operation Savage Glory.
Complete Operation Savage Glory - it carries the Snow Storm trophy inside this chapter.
Expect the story's highest wanted levels here; stock armour and ammo before each marker.
Finish any open stranger strand finals now; the endgame is a poor place to start them.
Audit the at-risk list before the chapter closes: strand finals and partner trophies first.
Keep the pre-finale master save separate from your rolling chapter saves.
Play the closing missions to the chapter end; the trophy pops as Chapter 4 completes.
Hidden on PSN until earned, as with the other chapter trophies.
Your 100 percent checklist should now show only endgame and grind items open.
After this pops, only the final mission stands between you and the story gold.
Update the tracker stage to Finale before starting the last mission.

dispute.a: One finale guide says a single ending choice changes which trophy-adjacent scene plays.
dispute.b: Another says the choice is cosmetic and the trophy pops identically on every path.
dispute.call: The trophy itself is safe on every path - it rewards completing the final mission, full stop. Keep a pre-finale save if you want to see the other scene.

trophies.guide: Finish the game's final mission. This is one of only two gold trophies on the list, it is story-gated, and it pops at the mission-complete screen after the finale.
trophies.missableWindow: Keep a save before starting the final mission so ending-adjacent cleanup stays reachable.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off

steps.text: Start the final mission only after the at-risk audit: strand finals done, partner trophies done, meditations safe.
Make the master save in a separate slot before accepting the mission prompt; the game warns this is the point of no return for the story.
Bring full armour, full ammo and your best vehicle loadout; the finale chains several combat beats.
Play the mission to its end without skipping the closing scenes; the trophy is tied to full completion.
Make the ending choice the story offers; guides agree the trophy pops on every path.
The gold pops on the mission-complete screen after the finale resolves.
Roadmaps place this as the second-to-last trophy for most players, just before the platinum.
After the credits, free roam continues - use it for any counted grind still open.
If a strand final was left open, reload the master save rather than starting a new game.
Mark it earned: with 100 percent also done, the platinum follows.
This and A Long Road are the only golds - plan your final sessions around those two.

dispute.a: One walkthrough calls Breakfast Run a driving-only mission with no combat.
dispute.b: Another warns of a short on-foot beat where a fail is possible.
dispute.call: Go in expecting both: drive carefully, and if the on-foot beat appears, treat it as a normal checkpointed segment.

trophies.guide: Finish the Chapter 1 story mission Breakfast Run. It is on the required path, so simply playing the story earns it; the trophy pops at the mission-complete screen.
trophies.name: Trust

steps.text: Accept Breakfast Run when the marker appears early in Chapter 1; it follows Gone Fishing on the story path.
Drive the route the objective marks and stay in the vehicle when the game asks you to tail rather than chase.
Complete the drop-off beat and let the short cutscene finish; control returns in free roam.
The mission is required story content, so it cannot be skipped or locked out by side content.
The trophy pops at the mission-complete screen and is PSN-hidden until earned.
Use the free roam right after this mission to start the coastal meditation spots while Chapter 1 is young.
Two early meditation spots sit near this mission's route; visiting them now saves a later trip.
Roadmaps order this second overall - it is the natural second trophy of a platinum run.
If a fail state triggers, the checkpoint is at the drive's start; nothing trophy-related is lost.
Mark Trust earned and keep the Chapter 1 stage filter on.
No collectible or count is attached to this mission; it is pure story progress.

dispute.a: One heist guide says a loud approach changes a later contact's availability.
dispute.b: Another says approach choice only changes the take and dialogue, never availability.
dispute.call: We flag it at-risk out of caution: pick the approach you prefer, but keep a pre-heist save until the next chapter proves your contacts intact.

trophies.guide: Finish The Cartel Heist, the Chapter 1 set-piece. It is required story content; we flag it at-risk only because its approach choice is the last big decision before the Chapter 1 missable window closes.
trophies.missableWindow: Last chance: make your backup save before starting The Cartel Heist - the Chapter 1 meditation window closes as the chapter ends after it.
trophies.name: Break the Bank

steps.text: Start The Cartel Heist from its Chapter 1 marker once the build-up missions are done.
Before accepting, save in a fresh slot: this mission leads into the chapter close, where the meditation window shuts.
Confirm your Chapter 1 meditation spots are visited before you commit to the heist.
Pick your approach at the planning beat; both routes complete the mission and pay the trophy.
Play the heist beats in order - entry, vault, escape - following the marked objectives.
During the escape, switch drivers when prompted; the chase is scripted to loosen once you clear the marked zone.
Let the aftermath cutscene play; chapter-close events follow from it.
The trophy pops at the mission-complete screen; PSN-hidden until earned.
If you skipped the meditations, reload the pre-heist save now rather than after the chapter banner.
Roadmaps treat this as the Chapter 1 finale in practice, whatever the formal chapter count says.
Mark it earned and check the missables tab: Positive Mental Attitude should read safe or done.

dispute.a: One mission guide describes Child's Play as a gentle escort with generous checkpoints.
dispute.b: Another calls its middle drive the first real fail-risk of Chapter 2.
dispute.call: Drive the middle segment carefully and the disagreement never matters - checkpoints cover the rest.

trophies.guide: Finish the Chapter 2 story mission Child's Play. Required story content on the platinum path; the trophy pops when the mission completes.
trophies.name: Family Matters

steps.text: Pick up Child's Play from its Chapter 2 marker; it sits mid-chapter on the required path.
Follow the escort beats as scripted - staying close matters more than speed here.
Complete the playground and drive sequences in order and let the closing scene finish.
The mission cannot be declined permanently; leaving it just parks the marker for later.
Trophy pops at the mission-complete screen; hidden on PSN until earned.
Chapter 2 is a good chapter to pair story progress with the first drone race locations.
If a Top Fun drone marker is near this mission's area, clear it on the same trip.
No count or collectible is attached; this is pure story progress.
Keep the rolling chapter save habit: one fresh slot per chapter banner.
Mark Family Matters earned in the tracker.
Strand markers for Billy often appear around this point - start them when they do.

dispute.a: One mission guide says Headliners can be stealthed almost to the end.
dispute.b: Another says the set-piece turns loud at a fixed trigger whatever you do.
dispute.call: Start quiet and be ready for the loud turn; both readings agree the trophy only needs completion.

trophies.guide: Finish the Chapter 3 story mission Headliners. Required story content; the trophy name on PSN is DWNFALL and it pops at the mission-complete screen.
trophies.name: DWNFALL

steps.text: Start Headliners from its Chapter 3 marker when the story sends you to the venue.
Play the infiltration beat quietly until the script turns it loud; both halves are required.
Hold the marked position during the headline set-piece and follow the extraction objective.
Required story mission - it cannot be missed, only postponed.
The trophy pops under its PSN name DWNFALL at the mission-complete screen.
Chapter 3 pairs well with shooting range batches between story markers.
The range challenges near the venue district unlock by this point in most routes.
No collectible is hidden inside the mission itself; do not detour mid-mission.
Difficulty settings do not change this trophy.
Mark DWNFALL earned and continue the Chapter 3 chain.
VCIA Takedown usually follows soon after in the same chapter.

dispute.a: One airport guide says the unscheduled-departure trophy must be done during this mission.
dispute.b: Another says VCIA stays enterable in free roam, so the departure can be done any time after.
dispute.call: We plan the departure for free roam after the chapter, but doing it during the mission also works - just do not leave the airport region for good without trying it once.

trophies.guide: Finish the Chapter 3 story mission VCIA Takedown at the airport. Required story content; it also introduces the airport used by the Catch Me If You Can trophy.
trophies.missableWindow: Watch: the airport set-piece changes after this mission; the related departure trophy is safest attempted while VCIA is fresh.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked

steps.text: Start VCIA Takedown from its Chapter 3 airport marker.
Play the takedown beats in order - perimeter, terminal, runway - as the objectives update.
Use the service vehicles the mission provides; they are tuned for the runway chase.
Required story content; the trophy pops at completion regardless of approach.
PSN-hidden until earned, like the other named-mission trophies.
Note the airport layout while you are here - a later trophy uses an unscheduled departure from VCIA.
Video guides mark the departure point on the far runway; watch the route once before trying it.
No in-mission collectible competes for your attention; finish the mission cleanly.
Keep a save after this mission: the airport state is a useful cleanup anchor.
Mark Hi-Jacked earned in the tracker.
Operation Savage Glory in Chapter 4 is the next named-mission trophy after this.

dispute.a: One mission guide calls Savage Glory the hardest story mission in the game.
dispute.b: Another says the finale is harder and Savage Glory is only the longest.
dispute.call: Prepare for both claims: full kit, full ammo, and patience - completion is all the trophy asks.

trophies.guide: Finish the Chapter 4 story mission Operation Savage Glory. Required story content and the last named-mission trophy before the finale; it pops at the mission-complete screen.
trophies.name: Snow Storm

steps.text: Start Operation Savage Glory from its Chapter 4 marker when the chain converges.
Stock armour and heavy ammo first; this is the longest combat mission before the finale.
Push the marked objectives in order and use Combat Focus on the grouped waves.
Grouped waves here are also a fair place to practise for the Gunslinger trophy's five-in-one-focus.
Required story content - it cannot be missed or locked out.
Trophy pops at the mission-complete screen; PSN-hidden until earned.
After this mission the story is nearly done; shift focus to strand finals and counts.
Run the at-risk audit now: any strand not started belongs at the top of your list.
Save in the finale-prep slot once this pops.
Roadmaps count this as the last bronze of the pure story chain.
Mark Snow Storm earned; the Finale stage is next.

dispute.a: One checklist totals the 100 percent from story, strands, collectibles and activities only.
dispute.b: Another believes a small slice of one-off world events also counts toward the percentage.
dispute.call: We track both: finish the four big categories first, then sweep one-off events if the counter stalls below 100.

trophies.guide: Reach 100 percent on the in-game completion counter. One of two golds. It is a sum of story, strands, collectibles, activities and counts - this guide's roadmap is ordered so most of it is already done by the time you check.
trophies.missableWindow: Watch: nothing here is missable, but strand finals must be finished before the finale save becomes your only anchor.
trophies.name: A Long Road

steps.text: Open the in-game 100 percent checklist from the pause menu and compare it line by line with this tracker.
Finish all story missions and chapters first; they form the largest single block of the percentage.
Complete all 8 stranger strands, not just the five with named final-mission trophies.
Sweep the collectible categories: card sets, WAiNK spots and meditation spots all feed the counter.
Try every activity type at least once; unplayed activity types are a common missing sliver.
Complete challenges beyond the 50 the trophy asks for if the counter needs them.
Visit every region of Leonida; unexplored areas can hold the last fraction.
Use a checklist tracker side by side with the game counter and reconcile after each session.
If the counter stalls at 99 percent, the usual suspects are one card set card and one activity type.
Roadmaps schedule this as the final grind before the finale gold for most players.
The gold pops the moment the counter reaches 100 percent, wherever you are standing.
Mark it earned; only the final mission and the platinum should remain.

dispute.a: One stunt guide counts only marked stunt jumps toward the 250.
dispute.b: Another counts any stunt the game registers - jumps, flips and near-miss bonuses - toward the same total.
dispute.call: We farm marked stunt locations first because they always register, then let ambient stunts top the count up.

trophies.guide: Register 250 stunts of any kind. A silver grind best done steadily: clear marked stunt spots whenever you pass one and the total builds itself across the platinum run.
trophies.missableWindow: Watch: stunt spots never close, but learning them alongside story travel is far faster than a cold endgame sweep.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts

steps.text: Learn what registers: the game flashes a stunt confirmation for jumps, flips and clean landings off ramps and drops.
Work the marked stunt locations district by district; each one can be repeated until it registers cleanly.
Watch one video route per district before farming it; stunt lines are much easier copied than discovered.
Use a light, fast vehicle class for ramp work - heavy vehicles under-rotate and fail the landing check.
Bank stunts opportunistically: one or two per story trip keeps this off your endgame list.
Tick locations off in the tracker as they register; the counter only shows the total, not which spots are done.
A failed landing still teaches the line; retry immediately while the approach is fresh.
Rain makes several ramps harder to read; farm stunt districts in clear weather where you can.
Stunts also feed the 100 percent counter, so this grind is never wasted time.
Expect the silver to pop mid-farm rather than at a set location - the 250th registered stunt is the trigger.
If the count stalls, change districts: repeated identical stunts in one spot are the usual suspect.

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.

dispute.a: One activity guide lists 9 types, matching the count in the official list's early summaries.
dispute.b: Another argues a tenth type unlocks late and is also required.
dispute.call: We track 9 from the official summaries and flag the rumoured tenth the moment any tracker shows it; trying a new type once costs minutes.

trophies.guide: Try every activity type once - 9 types by the official summaries. A sampler trophy: start one of each activity and this pops when the last new type registers.
trophies.name: Master of None

steps.text: Open the activities list and note the types: races, fishing, arcade games, shooting range, drone races, hunting, bowling, meditation and challenges are the tracked nine.
Start one activity of each type; you only need to try it, not win or finish it, for the type to register.
Tick each type off in this tracker as you go - the game does not show a per-type checklist.
Several types are introduced by story missions; if a type is greyed out, progress the story and return.
Fishing registers at any fishing spot once you cast; you do not need to beat Cal for this trophy.
Arcade registers when you complete a cabinet game session, which also covers Stick Fiddler.
Drone racing registers at your first Top Fun start, win or lose.
The shooting range registers on your first completed challenge card.
Meditation registers at your first completed spot sit.
The trophy pops when the ninth distinct type registers.
Every type tried also feeds 100 percent, so do this early in Chapter 2.

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.

dispute.a: One range guide says gold thresholds are fixed scores per challenge.
dispute.b: Another says a few challenges grade on accuracy percentage instead of raw score.
dispute.call: We play every challenge for both: fast and accurate. If a card resists, check which grading it uses before grinding it.

trophies.guide: Earn gold in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. A silver skill grind: learn each card's target pattern, use the range's own weapons, and gold the cards in batches across the story.
trophies.missableWindow: Watch: the range never closes, but its later cards unlock with story progress - gold them in batches as they open.
trophies.name: The Shootist

steps.text: Find the shooting range and open its challenge list: 42 cards across the weapon classes.
Start with the pistol cards to learn the scoring rhythm - targets reward speed chained with accuracy.
Use the range-provided weapons; personal loadouts do not carry into challenge scoring.
Replay a card immediately after a silver: the target pattern is fixed, so the second run is a memory test.
Watch a gold run of any card you cannot crack; most have one target order that makes the threshold comfortable.
Batch the work: five cards per range visit across Chapters 3 and 4 beats one endgame marathon.
Track golds in the stepper here; the game shows medals per card but no single gold total on the hub screen.
For accuracy-graded cards, slow down: a deliberate clean run out-scores a fast sloppy one.
Range golds also count toward 100 percent completion activities.
The silver pops when the 42nd card turns gold.
If a card seems bugged, leave and re-enter the range; trackers report medal saves happen on exit.

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.

dispute.a: One race guide lists 14 Top Fun locations, matching the early official summaries.
dispute.b: Another claims a 15th location appears after the finale.
dispute.call: We race the 14 confirmed locations; if a 15th appears post-finale we will add it - winning the known 14 is the requirement every list agrees on.

trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at all 14 locations. You must win, not just enter - but each course is short, fixed and learnable, and the races stay open all game.
trophies.name: Top Fun

steps.text: Find the Top Fun markers: 14 drone race locations spread across Leonida's districts.
Enter a race and learn its gate order on a sighting run; winning usually comes on run two or three.
Cut gates tight but centred - clipping a gate edge slows you more than a slightly wider line.
Video routes show the fastest line per course; copy the line, not the aggression.
Clear races as you travel for story missions; most districts hold one or two.
Tick each location in the tracker as you win it; the game lists locations but not at a glance.
A loss costs nothing but time - restart instantly while the course is fresh in your hands.
Wind affects later courses; if a coastal course frustrates, return in calmer weather.
Race wins also count toward the 20 different races needed for Earn Cash, Not Kudos where the lists overlap.
Keep the drone races separate in your count from street races; both trophies track differently.
The trophy pops on your 14th location win.

dispute.a: One race guide counts drone races inside the 20 different races.
dispute.b: Another counts only vehicle races - street, off-road and sea - toward the 20.
dispute.call: We win 20 vehicle races and treat drone wins as their own trophy; if drones do count, you simply finish sooner.

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. Different is the key word: 20 distinct events, not the same event 20 times. Mix street, off-road and sea races as they unlock across the map.
trophies.missableWindow: Watch: race events unlock by district and story progress, so the full 20 only opens up late - start early and finish late.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos

steps.text: Open the race list and count distinct events: you need wins at 20 different ones.
Start with the early street races near the starting districts; their fields are the slowest.
Bring a vehicle in the event's class with the best acceleration you own; top speed rarely decides these.
Learn each course once at cruising speed if it allows free entry, then race it properly.
Win races as you unlock districts so the last few are not a single endgame block.
Tick each distinct win in the tracker; repeats do not advance this count.
Off-road events reward grip over power - choose tyres and vehicle accordingly.
A loss never locks an event; re-enter immediately with the course fresh.
Race wins feed 100 percent and the activity sampler as well.
The trophy pops on your 20th distinct win.
If you are short late, check sea races - they are the most commonly forgotten category.

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.

dispute.a: One fishing guide says Cal's challenge difficulty scales with your fishing level.
dispute.b: Another says Cal is fixed and only your tackle changes the fight.
dispute.call: Either way the recipe is the same: upgrade tackle first, then take the challenge in calm morning water.

trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Find Cal's challenge at the fishing spots, bring decent tackle, and land a better catch than his within the challenge rules.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle

steps.text: Find a fishing spot and speak to Cal, or accept his challenge from the spot's board.
Practise the cast-and-reel rhythm on ordinary fish first; the challenge uses the same mechanics under a target.
Upgrade your rod and line at a tackle shop before the serious attempt; gear is cheap relative to story income.
Fish the challenge in the morning window the spot recommends; activity peaks change what bites.
Play the fish patiently - line tension breaks come from reeling against the run, not from the fish's size.
A short video of a winning catch shows the tension rhythm better than any text; watch one before your attempt.
Losing costs nothing but the entry moment; re-challenge immediately.
The trophy pops when the challenge result confirms you beat Cal's catch.
Fishing also registers the fishing activity type for Master of None.
Mark it earned; Cal's other role in the 100 percent list is separate from this trophy.
If the challenge will not start, progress the story a mission or two - some spots gate behind Chapter 2.

dispute.a: One cabinet guide says any cabinet game's completion counts.
dispute.b: Another says only full arcade cabinets count, not bar-top machines.
dispute.call: Use a full cabinet in an arcade first; it satisfies both readings and takes the same few minutes.

trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game at any cabinet. The shortest trophy on the list: find a cabinet, play its game through to completion once, and this pops.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler

steps.text: Find an arcade cabinet - arcades and bars across the map hold them, each with its own short game.
Pick the shortest cabinet game on offer; completion, not score, is the requirement.
Play the game to its actual end screen; quitting at a game-over does not count as completing it.
If a cabinet's game has a trick stage, a two-minute video clears it faster than trial and error.
Do this in Chapter 2 free roam; it takes minutes and clears an activity type too.
Arcade play registers the arcade activity type for Master of None at the same time.
The trophy pops on the completion screen of the cabinet game.
Mark it earned - there is no count or set attached to arcades beyond this.
Some cabinets only power on at certain hours; if one is dark, try another district or hour.
One completed cabinet game is also the arcade line of the 100 percent checklist.
No difficulty setting affects this trophy.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.

dispute.a: One strand guide says Andy's strand can be finished any time, even after the finale, from the post-game map.
dispute.b: Another says his final mission stops being offered once the endgame begins.

trophies.missableWindow: Last chance: finish Andy's final mission before starting the game's final mission.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation

steps.text: Find Andy's first strand marker when it appears during Chapter 2 and introduce yourself.
Work each strand stage as it unlocks; stages often gate behind a day passing or a story mission.
If a stage will not trigger, sleep or advance time in-game and return to the marker.
Strand stages are marked with the stranger's initial on the map once the strand is open.
Finish the final mission before the endgame: strand finals are the classic at-risk category in this list.
The trophy pops when Andy's final mission completes, not at earlier stages.
This trophy is PSN-hidden until earned; its blank card is normal.
Andy's strand also counts as one of the 8 strands for Strangers & Freaks and toward 100 percent.
Keep the strand's last save until the trophy confirms - a completion without a pop is a sync issue to reload.
Mark it earned and move to the next strand final in roadmap order.
No choice inside the strand changes the trophy; only completion matters.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.

dispute.a: One strand guide places Kenton's unlock in Chapter 2.
dispute.b: Another says his first marker only appears in Chapter 3 despite his strand being listed earlier.

trophies.guide: Complete Kenton's stranger strand through to its final mission. As with all strand finals, start early, finish before the endgame, and the trophy pops at the final mission's completion.
trophies.missableWindow: Last chance: finish Kenton's final mission before starting the game's final mission.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident

steps.text: Watch for Kenton's strand marker near the water districts from Chapter 2 onward.
Complete each stage as it unlocks; his strand leans on boat work, so bring patience for docking beats.
Advance time or finish a story mission if the next stage marker delays.
His strand touches the coast - combine stage trips with nearby exploration for The Goodtime State.
Finish his final mission before the endgame to keep it safe.
The trophy pops at the final mission's completion screen.
PSN-hidden until earned, like the other strand-final trophies.
Counts toward the 8 strands and 100 percent as well.
If a stage boat is destroyed, the stage restarts from its checkpoint; no strand progress is lost.
Mark earned and continue the strand order.
Choices inside the strand do not change the trophy outcome.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.

dispute.a: One strand guide says Billy's stages must be done in one in-game week.
dispute.b: Another says his strand has no clock at all and stages wait indefinitely.
dispute.call: We keep his stages moving between story missions anyway; a strand in motion is safe under either reading.

trophies.guide: Complete Billy's stranger strand through to its final mission. Start it when the marker appears, keep the stages moving between story missions, and close it out before the finale.
trophies.missableWindow: Last chance: finish Billy's final mission before starting the game's final mission.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider

steps.text: Find Billy's strand marker - his strand is road-themed and starts near the highway districts.
Work the stages in order; several involve driving his route within a generous time window.
Use a balanced vehicle for his stages: fast enough for the windows, sturdy enough for traffic.
Advance time in-game if a follow-up stage does not appear immediately.
Close the strand with its final mission before the endgame.
Trophy pops at the final mission's completion.
PSN-hidden until earned.
One of the 8 strands for Strangers & Freaks and part of 100 percent.
Stage failures restart at checkpoints; the strand itself cannot be failed permanently.
Mark earned in the tracker.
No collectible hides inside his stages; focus on completion.

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.

dispute.a: One strand census counts exactly 8 strands in the game, so this trophy means all of them.
dispute.b: Another counts more than 8 strands, making this a pick-any-8 trophy.
dispute.call: We complete the five named strands plus every other strand we find; either reading is covered by finishing them all.

trophies.guide: Complete 8 stranger mission strands anywhere in Leonida. A silver that mostly completes itself if you run every strand you meet: the five named finals (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) plus three more strands.
trophies.missableWindow: Watch: strands unlock across chapters; leaving them all to the endgame risks the at-risk finals crowding the finale.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks

steps.text: Understand the shape: a strand is a chain of missions for one stranger, ending in a final mission.
Start every strand the day its marker appears; an unstarted strand is the easiest thing to forget.
The named five - Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone - each carry their own final-mission trophy.
Three further strands have no trophy of their own but count toward this silver and 100 percent.
Keep strands moving between story missions so their stages unlock steadily.
Finish all strand finals before the finale; that habit makes this silver safe by construction.
Track strands in the stepper here - the game counts strands, not stages, and shows no hub list.
Every strand also feeds the 100 percent counter.
If a strand stalls, its next stage usually needs time passed or a chapter advanced.
The silver pops when the 8th strand's final mission completes.
Mark earned; the individual strand trophies should already be in hand.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.

dispute.a: One strand guide says Randy's strand pays out only if you front his costs promptly.
dispute.b: Another says the payments are scripted and timing changes nothing.
dispute.call: Front the costs when asked if you can afford it - it is the safe reading and the money returns through the strand.

trophies.guide: Complete Randy's stranger strand through to its final mission. His strand is the supply-chain one: start it early, run its stages between story beats, and finish it before the endgame.
trophies.missableWindow: Last chance: finish Randy's final mission before starting the game's final mission.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand

steps.text: Find Randy's strand marker when it appears and open the strand.
His stages revolve around moving goods; bring a vehicle with cargo room when a stage asks for a pickup.
Keep some cash spare during his strand - a stage may ask you to front money you later recover.
Advance time if the next stage marker is slow to appear.
Finish his final mission before the endgame.
Trophy pops at the final mission's completion.
Not hidden on PSN - this one shows on the public list from the start.
Counts toward the 8 strands and 100 percent.
Stage failures restart cleanly; the strand cannot be permanently failed.
Mark earned and move on in strand order.
His strand pairs well with the money trophies running in the background.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.

dispute.a: One strand guide says Tyrone's final mission needs a specific vehicle class delivered intact.
dispute.b: Another says any vehicle completes it and only the dialogue changes.
dispute.call: Deliver the requested class in good shape anyway - it costs nothing and covers the strict reading.

trophies.guide: Complete Tyrone's stranger strand through to its final mission. The last of the five named strand finals in roadmap order; finish it before the finale like the others.
trophies.missableWindow: Last chance: finish Tyrone's final mission before starting the game's final mission.
trophies.name: Spin On This!

steps.text: Find Tyrone's strand marker and open the strand when it appears.
Work his stages between story missions; they lean on driving and delivery beats.
Keep a mid-range car garaged for his stages - balanced speed and durability.
Pass time in-game if a stage follow-up delays.
Finish the final mission before the endgame begins.
Trophy pops at the final mission's completion.
Shows on the public list; not a hidden trophy.
Counts toward the 8 strands and 100 percent.
Checkpoints inside stages make failures cheap.
With this earned, all five named strand finals should be complete.
Only completion matters; strand choices do not alter the trophy.

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.

dispute.a: PowerPyx counts 18 meditation spots and says two Chapter 1 coastal spots become unreachable once Chapter 1 closes, because the story moves the camp.
dispute.b: PSNProfiles counts 18 spots too but says every spot stays reachable all game, and the missable label comes from a balcony spot tied to a Chapter 1 property you can lose access to.
dispute.call: We do not gamble on which reading is right: clear every Chapter 1 spot before The Cartel Heist ends the chapter, then finish the rest in free roam. Both readings are safe under that order.

trophies.guide: Meditate at every meditation spot in Leonida - 18 spots by the count both big registries use. This is the list's one possibly-missable trophy: a Chapter 1 window closes as the chapter ends, so clear the early coastal spots before The Cartel Heist wraps up, then finish the rest in free roam.
trophies.missableWindow: Last chance: the Chapter 1 spots must be visited before The Cartel Heist ends Chapter 1 - after the chapter closes, the early camp moves and the coastal spots tied to it are gone on the stricter reading.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude

steps.text: Learn the count first: registries agree on 18 meditation spots across Leonida, even where they disagree on the window.
Treat this as the run's one true deadline: Chapter 1 spots before The Cartel Heist closes the chapter.
Spot 1 sits near the Gone Fishing coast; visit it in the free roam right after the opening mission.
Spots are marked by a small mat and incense at viewpoints - beaches, a pier end, hilltops and one balcony.
Sit at each spot and let the full meditation finish; standing up early does not register the spot.
Clear the Chapter 1 coastal cluster - the spots around the early camp - before starting the heist.
Missable roundups single this trophy out as the list's one possibly-missable entry; plan around it, not around rumours.
Tick each spot in the stepper here as it registers; the game shows the total only inside this trophy's count.
The remaining spots unlock with the map: work them district by district as chapters open new ground.
Community reports flag the balcony spot as the awkward one - if it will not trigger, return at a different hour.
A video route of all 18 spots exists; use it for the final sweep if your count is short.
The trophy pops when the 18th spot registers - if you are at 17 after Chapter 1 with none left reachable, the pre-heist save is the fix.

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.

dispute.a: One hunting guide says the unique animal only appears at dawn in its territory.
dispute.b: Another says it is a scripted spawn tied to accepting Bret's request, at any hour.
dispute.call: Accept Bret's request first, then hunt at dawn anyway - that order satisfies both readings.

trophies.guide: Hunt the unique animal Bret asks for. Take his request, track the animal in its territory, and bring the hunt to a clean finish; the trophy pops when Bret's hunt resolves.
trophies.name: Fair Game

steps.text: Meet Bret and accept his hunting request; the unique animal is tied to his strand of hunting work.
Learn the animal's territory from the request notes before travelling - it roams one defined area.
Approach downwind and crouched; the wildlife system spooks unique animals faster than common ones.
A video of the hunt shows the approach line that keeps the animal from bolting.
Bring the appropriate hunting weapon the request implies; the wrong tool can fail the hunt's condition.
If the animal escapes, leave the area and return; unique spawns reset rather than vanish forever.
Hunting registers progress in the activities slice of 100 percent as well.
The trophy pops when the hunt resolves back to Bret.
No other trophy depends on this hunt's outcome.
Difficulty and aim settings do not affect the trophy.
Hunting also registers the hunting activity type for Master of None.

dispute.a: One card guide says set completion needs every card in the set found in the world.
dispute.b: Another says a small number of cards come from activities rather than world pickups.
dispute.call: We collect world cards set by set and check the activity-reward cards whenever a set sits one short.

trophies.guide: Complete 3 full Collectible Card sets. Not 3 cards - 3 whole sets. Work set by set with the tracker so partial sets never blur, and this silver lands well before a full collection would.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck

steps.text: Open the card collection screen and learn the set structure: cards belong to themed sets, and a set counts only when complete.
Pick the three smallest sets first; they finish fastest and bank the trophy early.
Work one set at a time district by district so your stepper notes match the game's set screen.
Cards glint at their spots - check counters, shelves and dock posts as you pass through interiors.
Video routes per set exist; use them for the last card of a set, which is always the hidden one.
Collect cards opportunistically during story travel; a dedicated sweep is the fallback, not the plan.
A card once taken is permanent - no card can be missed or lost.
Card sets also feed the collectibles slice of 100 percent.
The trophy pops when the third set completes, even if other sets are untouched.
If a set sits one short for long, check activity rewards - a few cards pay out from activities, not pickups.
You do not need every set in the game for this trophy; three complete sets is the whole requirement.

dispute.a: One location guide counts exactly 100 WAiNK spots in the world.
dispute.b: Another counts more than 100 spots and says any 100 of them satisfy the trophy.
dispute.call: We visit spots until the counter says 100; extra spots, if they exist, are a kindness, not a conflict.

trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK It action at 100 different locations. A silver counting grind: the spots are everywhere, they never close, and steady opportunistic visits finish it long before the endgame.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!

steps.text: Learn the action: certain marked spots across Leonida invite the WAiNK It prompt when you stand on them.
Each distinct location counts once; repeating a spot does not advance the counter.
Spots cluster in busy districts - beaches, boardwalks, marinas and viewpoints hold several each.
Tick districts off in the tracker as you clear them; the game shows only the running total.
Visit spots opportunistically on every story trip - five minutes of detours per session finishes this early.
A full video route exists for a final sweep if your count stalls in the nineties.
No spot is missable: none of the registries tie any location to a story window.
WAiNK spots count inside the collectibles slice of 100 percent.
If a prompt will not appear, adjust your stance on the marker - the trigger is positional and small.
The silver pops on the 100th distinct location.
Mark earned; there is no bonus trophy for spots beyond 100.

dispute.a: One challenges guide says the game holds exactly 50 challenges, so this means all of them.
dispute.b: Another lists more than 50 challenges across categories, making this a choose-your-50 trophy.
dispute.call: We complete the shortest challenges first across every category; if the pool is exactly 50, that order still finishes the list.

trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges from the game's challenge lists. Work the short categories first - many challenges complete passively while you play for other trophies.
trophies.missableWindow: Watch: a few challenges are easier inside their story windows; the bulk are free-roam and never close.
trophies.name: One Last Thing

steps.text: Open the challenges hub and survey the categories: driving, combat, exploration, economy and more.
Start with passive challenges - distance, spending and discovery ones complete while you play normally.
Pick short active challenges next; many are single-action tasks dressed as a list.
Let this trophy ride along with the others: check the hub at each session's end and claim what finished.
Track your 50 in the stepper here; the hub shows per-challenge state, not one clean total.
Challenges completed also feed 100 percent, so none of this work is wasted.
No challenge is missable in the registries' reading; a stalled challenge is a hidden condition, not a closed one.
Video walkthroughs cover the handful of challenges with non-obvious triggers.
The trophy pops on the 50th completed challenge.
If the pool is larger than 50, stop at 50 - the rest belong to 100 percent only.
Revisit the hub after the finale; late challenges unlock with endgame content.

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.

dispute.a: One partner guide reads this as a co-op trophy needing a second player online.
dispute.b: Another reads partner as the story's second protagonist, making it a solo trophy with the AI partner present.
dispute.call: We plan it solo with the story partner beside you - the official description says partner, not online - and it needs no online play on that reading.

trophies.guide: Reach a 4-star wanted level with your partner present, then lose the heat completely. Plan it somewhere with a fast escape route and a vehicle swap, and let the stars drain to zero.
trophies.missableWindow: Last chance: partner availability follows the story - attempt this while both protagonists are together in free roam, well before the finale.
trophies.name: Hot Together

steps.text: Set up in free roam with your partner present; the trophy's condition needs the partner alongside when the heat drops.
Pick an escape-friendly district: alleys, a vehicle swap and a hiding route within a short drive.
Raise your wanted level deliberately to exactly 4 stars with quick, contained offences.
Do not push to 5 stars - the requirement is a 4-star escape, and higher heat only adds risk.
Break line of sight first, then swap vehicles out of sight; video routes show reliable drain spots per district.
Stay hidden while the stars blink down; re-entering a search cone restarts the drain.
The trophy pops when the wanted level clears completely with the partner still with you.
Attempt this well before the finale, while partner free-roam time is plentiful.
If the partner wanders off mid-escape, regroup and restart the raise; the condition is checked at the escape.
Wanted escapes do not feed other counters - this is a standalone set-piece.
No online connection is needed on the story-partner reading; it is a campaign trophy.

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.

dispute.a: One guide says back-to-back means the wanted level must never fully clear between shops.
dispute.b: Another says it means one continuous spree with no arrest, bust or wasted in between, wanted level free to fluctuate.
dispute.call: We play the stricter reading: keep the heat alive between all three shops and the trophy is safe under both.

trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops in one continuous spree with your partner, keeping your wanted level alive between them. Route three close shops beforehand, move fast, and never let the heat fully die until the third till is empty.
trophies.missableWindow: Last chance: attempt while both protagonists are together in free roam, before the finale separates the story.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy

steps.text: Scout a cluster of three shops within a short drive of each other before starting.
Bring your partner and a fast, durable car; the spree is a driving problem more than a shooting one.
Rob shop one: take the till, leave as the wanted level rises, and drive straight to shop two.
Keep the wanted level alive between shops - do not hide long enough for it to clear.
Rob shop two the same way and move immediately; lingering is what breaks the chain.
Rob shop three and only then break line of sight and escape properly.
Video runs show two reliable shop clusters; copy a cluster rather than improvising a route.
The trophy pops when the third robbery registers with the chain intact.
Do this during partner free-roam time, well before the finale.
Getting busted or wasted mid-spree ends the attempt; restart from shop one.
Shop robberies also feed the economy side of the challenge lists.

dispute.a: One vehicle guide says discovery means entering a vehicle model for the first time.
dispute.b: Another says discovery registers when the model is scanned or seen up close in traffic.
dispute.call: We enter every new model we see - entering satisfies both readings and builds your garage knowledge anyway.

trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles. Discovery is about variety, not ownership: enter or register new models as you meet them in traffic and this completes itself across a normal playthrough.
trophies.name: Whip It Good

steps.text: Learn the rule: each distinct vehicle model counts once, the first time you discover it.
Enter every unfamiliar car, bike, boat and aircraft you pass; a second in the seat is enough on the entering reading.
Different districts spawn different traffic - new areas are discovery goldmines.
Let this build passively: by Chapter 3 most players are past halfway without trying.
Track the count in the stepper; the game shows discovered models in its vehicle index.
Garaged and purchased vehicles count too, so property purchases push this along.
Rare models hide in rich districts and at the airport; sweep those when the count slows.
Vehicle discovery feeds the exploration slice of 100 percent.
Video lists of rare spawn points exist for the last stubborn models.
The trophy pops on the 100th distinct model.
Registering vehicles in the Scooter Bros app is a separate trophy - do not confuse the two counts.

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.

dispute.a: One combat guide says takedowns must be lethal to count inside the Focus window.
dispute.b: Another says any downed enemy, lethal or not, counts toward the five.
dispute.call: Go lethal for the attempt - it satisfies the strict reading and ends fights faster anyway.

trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies during one Combat Focus activation. Wait for a grouped wave - the Savage Glory mission and heist escapes offer natural clusters - then trigger Focus and drop five before it ends.
trophies.name: Gunslinger

steps.text: Learn Combat Focus: it slows the fight briefly and is built for exactly this kind of cluster.
Do not waste attempts on scattered pairs; wait for a wave of five or more in one space.
Operation Savage Glory and heist escapes both throw grouped waves at you - prime windows.
Range practice helps: target-switching speed is the whole skill here.
Line up the group, trigger Focus, and work nearest to farthest without reloading mid-window.
A video attempt shows the timing - most players pop it on their first deliberate try in a big wave.
PSN-hidden until earned; do not worry that it hides from public lists.
The trophy pops as the fifth takedown lands inside the same Focus use.
If a wave thins early, hold Focus for the next one rather than forcing it.
Combat challenges in the hub overlap this skill set.
Difficulty does not change the count - five is five on any setting.

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.

dispute.a: One airport guide says any stolen aircraft departure from VCIA counts.
dispute.b: Another says it must be a specific parked aircraft on the far runway, outside the mission context.
dispute.call: Try a free-roam departure from the far runway first; if it does not pop, take any aircraft out in free roam - between them both readings are covered in minutes.

trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure from VCIA airport: get airborne in an aircraft you were never cleared to take. Easiest in free roam after the takedown mission opens the airport up.
trophies.missableWindow: Watch: the airport is most open right after VCIA Takedown in Chapter 3 - attempt it in that window first.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can

steps.text: Return to VCIA in free roam after completing VCIA Takedown in Chapter 3.
Head for the far runway's parked aircraft - the departure point video guides use.
Enter the aircraft without any mission or job active; unscheduled is the operative word.
Taxi out and take off cleanly; the trophy checks the departure, not the flight that follows.
The trophy pops shortly after wheels-up if the departure registered.
If it does not pop, land, leave the airport fully, and repeat with a different parked aircraft.
PSN-hidden until earned.
Community reports say a wanted level is not required - do not raise heat you do not need.
Doing this during the takedown mission itself is unreliable; free roam is the planned route.
The flight also discovers the aircraft model for Whip It Good if it is new to you.
Mark earned and leave the airport before security escalates.

dispute.a: One guide reads the joke description as surviving inside a stolen Rhino tank for a set stretch.
dispute.b: Another reads it as taking down a Rhino with another vehicle or heavy weapon.
dispute.call: Start by stealing and holding a Rhino - survival first. If the pop does not come, escalate to destroying one on the next attempt.

trophies.guide: The joke description points at the Rhino tank: get into one and stay in the heat, or bring one down - the registries disagree on the exact verb, so this guide walks the survival route first and the destruction route second.
trophies.missableWindow: Watch: Rhinos only roll out at high wanted levels or military sites - attempt when your arsenal and armour are ready.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank

steps.text: Learn where Rhinos appear: at the highest wanted levels and around military ground.
Prepare first - full armour, a heavy weapon and an escape vehicle staged nearby.
Raise your wanted level in a controlled area until armour rolls out, or approach the military site directly.
Video attempts show the boarding window: disable or distract the crew side, then take the hatch.
Once inside a Rhino, stay in it and survive the heat for a stretch - the survival reading's condition.
If the trophy has not popped after a solid survival stretch, switch to the destruction reading.
For destruction, use the heaviest ordnance you own from hard cover and keep moving between shots.
PSN-hidden until earned, which suits a joke-description trophy.
Either way, escape or clear the heat afterwards; the trophy saves at the pop, not at the escape.
Expect this to take two or three attempts while you learn Rhino behaviour.
Tank encounters also feed combat challenge progress.

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.

dispute.a: One stealth guide says detection means a full alarm - a filled meter that resets is fine.
dispute.b: Another says any guard suspicion state voids the attempt.
dispute.call: Play the strict reading: if anyone's meter even fills, leave, let the store reset, and run it perfectly next time.

trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store in complete stealth: no detection from entry to exit. Scout the store, go in quiet with the right tools, empty the cases and leave before anyone raises the alarm.
trophies.missableWindow: Watch: stores restock and reset daily, so a failed attempt is retried the next in-game day - nothing closes permanently.
trophies.name: Sneakthief

steps.text: Pick a jewelry store and scout it first: entrances, staff positions and the case layout.
Go in with a quiet loadout - the stealth reading punishes noise, not slowness.
Enter outside peak hours where the store allows it; fewer witnesses means fewer detection chances.
Video runs show the staff-sightline rhythm; wait for the look-away beats before moving.
Empty the marked cases without breaking glass loudly where the quiet method is offered.
If a detection meter fills, freeze - most meters drain if you stop moving immediately.
Leave by the entry you scouted and walk, do not run, until you are clear of the door.
The trophy pops once you are clear with the take and no detection registered.
A detected attempt is not a lockout: return the next in-game day and try the same store again.
This pairs naturally with Retail Therapy scouting, but do not combine the attempts - stealth first, spree another day.
Store robberies feed the economy challenges too.

dispute.a: One robbery guide says only the five named bank branches with vaults count.
dispute.b: Another says any bank vault, including the smaller branches, counts toward the five.
dispute.call: We rob the five named vault branches first; if the counter moves on a small branch too, that is a bonus, never a problem.

trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape cleanly each time. A silver built from repetition: learn one clean vault route, then run it across five branches with an escape plan staged before you go in.
trophies.missableWindow: Watch: vaults reset over time, so this is repeatable - but branch access follows story progress.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal

steps.text: Learn the vault loop: entry, vault access, take, escape - the escape is part of the requirement, not an extra.
Stage the escape before entering: a fast car parked discreetly and a route with a vehicle swap.
Rob the first named branch and escape fully - wanted level cleared - to bank vault one.
Track vaults in the stepper; the game does not show a clean vault counter in the hub.
Repeat across branches as they open with story progress rather than forcing one branch repeatedly.
Video routes exist per branch; the vault interiors differ enough to be worth a look first.
Getting busted after the vault but before escape voids that vault's count on the strict reading - escape properly.
Alternate districts between vaults to keep heat patterns varied and manageable.
Vault money accelerates the spending and laundering trophies running alongside.
The silver pops on the fifth successful vault-and-escape.
Mark earned; extra vaults remain good income for garages.

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.

dispute.a: One robbery guide says the truck must be cracked with the breaching tool for the trophy.
dispute.b: Another says any method of opening the truck and escaping with the take counts.
dispute.call: Bring the breaching tool - it is the documented method and the fastest either way.

trophies.guide: Rob one armored truck and escape. Ambush it on a quiet stretch, crack it fast with the right tool, take the money and lose the heat - one clean job is the whole trophy.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play

steps.text: Armored trucks run routes in free roam; learn one route and pick a quiet ambush stretch on it.
Bring the breaching tool the truck's doors require - check your inventory before the ambush, not during.
Stop the truck with a vehicle block rather than a chase; a stopped truck is a fast truck.
Video attempts show the door timing - the breach window is generous once the truck is halted.
Take the money and move immediately; the escape timer in your head starts at the breach.
The trophy pops when you clear the wanted level with the take secured.
If the truck escapes, another runs the route later - trucks are a renewable event.
Do not combine this with the Retail Therapy spree; the truck's heat spike breaks shop chains.
The take feeds your cash pool for spending and garage trophies.
One truck is enough - repeats are income, not progress.
Community notes say rain empties the ambush stretch of witnesses, making the escape simpler.

dispute.a: One exploration guide counts 52 named areas that must each be entered.
dispute.b: Another counts the same 52 but says a few register only on foot, not from a vehicle.
dispute.call: We sweep area by area and step out of the vehicle at each area's landmark - that satisfies both readings at once.

trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida - 52 areas by the count the official summaries carry. A map-completion trophy that finishes naturally if you sweep each new district on foot at its landmark as the story opens the state.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State

steps.text: Open the map and learn the area structure: 52 named areas make up the state of Leonida.
As each district opens, drive its length once, then step out at its landmark so the area registers on foot too.
Fast travel helps you reposition, but areas only register when you are physically present in them.
Shade cleared areas in the tracker; the in-game map fog shows visited ground but not a clean area count.
